Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you
reported in Pasadena, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give my first name for now, if that's all right.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving and what the traffic was like?
A: I was heading east on a main road in the late afternoon. Traffic had slowed to a crawl near a shopping center, so I
was stopped behind a sedan at a light.
Q: What happened next?
A: The light was still red when I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped fowrard and then back against the
headrest. The car behind me had hit me, and I could see the other driver's bumper right in my mirror.
Q: Did you exit your vehicle or speak with the other driver?
A: I got out and walked around. The other driver said they had looked down at their phone for a second. We
exchanged information, and an officer came out to take a report.
Q: Did you seek medical attention after the collision?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. My neck was stiff and sore, and by the next morning I had pain running
into my shoulders and a headache. The doctor told me it looked like whiplash and gave me a referral for physical
therapy.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms today?
A: Yes. Turning my head to check blind spots is painful, and I've had trouble sleeping. I'm attending therapy twice a
week, and I've had to limit how long I sit at my desk.
Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just want my car repaired and my recovery handled properly.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
